concerns.text: Phase 6 introduces tasks T031-T042 (Blind Agent, Decay, Consolidation, Noise, Scaling Exponent) driven by external reviewer comments. These tasks have no corresponding Functional Requirement (FR) or Success Criterion (SC) in spec.md, nor are they listed in plan.md (which explicitly states 'Phase 7 tasks... were removed'). The implementer cannot satisfy these requirements as they are not defined in the source spec/plan, creating a coverage gap where tasks exist without spec backing.

Task T015b enforces N=1000 games for power analysis. While FR-009 mentions N=1000, the plan.md explicitly sets the default execution budget to N=200 for CPU runs and requires the system to 'flag a limitation' if power < 0.70 for the *planned* design. T015b bypasses the requirement to test the *actual* planned design (N=200) by hard-coding a high-N run, leaving the spec requirement to 'estimate detectable effect size for the planned N' (where planned N=200) without a dedicated task to perform that specific calculation on the default dataset.

Success Criterion SC-003 requires the sensitivity analysis to report the 'maximum absolute change in any metric between thresholds'. Task T022 only defines outputting a CSV with means (`mean_specialization`, `mean_retrieval`). There is no task explicitly defined to calculate and report the 'maximum absolute change' value, leaving SC-003 uncovered.

Tasks T031-T042 in Phase 6 reference external reviewers (Turing, Rockmore, etc.) and introduce new logic (Blind Agent, Decay, Consolidation) that are not present in spec.md or plan.md. These tasks appear to be stale or orphaned from a previous iteration or external feedback loop that was not integrated into the current spec/plan. They should be either removed or the spec/plan must be updated to include these as formal requirements.
